Return statuses with share above that average. Show status, count, share, and share minus average share (absolute difference).
Same as 1, but "how far above the average" is the ratio of share to average share (share / average), not the difference.
Same as 1, but "how far above" is the percentage difference relative to the average, i.e. (share − average) / average × 100.

Same as 1, but the average share is the arithmetic mean of the per-status shares computed in the query (AVG of the share column). This gives the same value as 1/N, so it is the same result by a different calculation.
Same as 1, but the missing-status group means only NULL values. Empty strings are treated as a separate status.

Same as 1, but statuses are compared case-insensitively or after trimming whitespace. Variants like 'Verified' and 'verified' are merged into one group.
Same as 1, but the share is computed only over QC records linked to a valid project or operator (joined to `projects` or `personnel`), not over all `scanqc` rows.
Same as 1, with the "above average" cutoff taken as strictly greater than the average (as stated), versus greater than or equal to the average.
Same as 1, with results in a specified order, e.g. by share descending, or unordered.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT archstat AS status, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM scanqc
  GROUP BY archstat
),
t AS (
  SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM g
)
SELECT g.status,
       g.cnt AS count,
       CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total AS share,
       ABS(CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total - 1.0 / t.n) AS share_minus_avg_share
FROM g, t
WHERE CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total > 1.0 / t.n;
SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share
FROM (
  SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM equipment) AS share
  FROM equipment
  GROUP BY equipstatus
);
